about.title: Lompoc Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Lompoc's mix of small retail strips along H Street, apartment properties near O Street, and public walkways throughout the city means falls happen for a lot of different reasons — wet flooring, cracked pavement, poor lighting, or a hazard that was never fixed after someone reported it. Under California law, a property owner or manager can be held responsible only if they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and didn't fix it or warn people about it. That's why what happens right after your fall matters: photos of the hazard, names of any witnesses, and a request to preserve store or building surveillance footage can all make a real difference later. LawProactive doesn't represent you directly — we're a free service that connects injured Lompoc residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the details of your fall and explain your options, working on contingency so there's no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Lompoc Premises Case

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help gather the evidence needed to establish that notice.

items.title: Video Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Many properties overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that footage can be critical to your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar You
items.desc: California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover damages even if you were partly at fault for the fall — your share of fault simply adjusts the final amount.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Lompoc?
items.answer: In most cases you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit under California law. If the property involved is owned by a government entity — a city building or public sidewalk, for example — that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just a few months. Because of that difference, it's worth having someone review the details of where the fall happened as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell at a business on H Street or O Street and no one else saw it?
items.answer: Lack of witnesses doesn't automatically end a claim. Photos of the hazard, your own written account while it's fresh, and any store surveillance video can still support your case. An attorney connected through LawProactive can help identify what evidence is realistically available in your situation.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service — we're not a law firm and we don't charge for connecting you with an independent attorney. Attorneys in the network generally work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
